slides.title: Simplifying Context Managers with @contextmanager
slides.prompt: The `@contextmanager` decorator from `contextlib` converts a generator function into a context manager. Code before `yield` runs upon entering the context, `yield` provides the target value, and code after `yield` executes upon exit.

slides.title: Decorator Import Name
slides.prompt: Fill in the decorator function imported from `contextlib` to create generator-based context managers.

slides.title: Role of yield in @contextmanager
slides.prompt: What role does the `yield` statement play inside a `@contextmanager` generator function?
options: It separates setup code from teardown code and yields the bound target value
It converts the function into an infinite loop
It acts as a return statement for throwing errors
slides.correctAnswer: It separates setup code from teardown code and yields the bound target value

slides.title: Exception Trapping in Generators
slides.prompt: Fill in the block keyword wrapped around `yield` to catch exceptions raised within the `with` body.
slides.codeSnippet:
@contextmanager
def safe_resource():
    # setup
    ___:
        yield
    finally:
        # teardown

slides.title: Handling Exceptions inside Generator Contexts
slides.prompt: Where is an unhandled exception inside a `with` block re-raised inside a `@contextmanager` generator?
options: Directly at the location of the `yield` statement
At the beginning of the generator function
slides.correctAnswer: Directly at the location of the `yield` statement

slides.title: Yield Without Target Value
slides.prompt: Fill in the yield value used if the context manager does not produce an explicit object for the `as` clause.

slides.title: Generator Yield Limit
slides.prompt: How many times MUST a `@contextmanager` generator function yield during a single context execution?
options: As many times as requested by a loop
